findings: Exactly one used-macro Binding per case; repeated ADD and shared VALUE calls do not multiply it. UNUSED has no METHOD or Binding in its control.
Every macro Binding has exactly three string properties; one incoming BINDS and one outgoing REF with null payloads.

Retained header macro binds from main.c:<global>; shared two-caller macro binds from a.c:<global> although its FULL_NAME starts shared.h. This observed owner must not be inferred from the header prefix.
Four macro Binding components are missing in accepted Rust. Full214/756 Joern vs210/578 Rust remains nonexact despite four complete canonical byte matches.
This is observed four-case evidence, not a universal first-file ownership rule, source implementation review or final candidate acceptance.
